compatibility_evidence: 2026-11-07: data-dictionary/PRDs/011-dictionary-sync (Kaynak bağlantı noktası). Direct runtime pin pymssql 2.4.6 in app/backend/requirements.in (PyPI upload 2026-10-27, licence metadata GNU Lesser General Public License; musllinux_1_2 x86_64 cp314 wheel sha256 7177bc90667a9d89bafbd9ccc44b5db20baea47f4b0737556b501aa489787f74, which bundles FreeTDS 1.5.19, OpenSSL and Kerberos libraries); the SQL Server dictionary source adapter imports it. It has no Python dependency, so the three locks gain only this package and its PyPI digests. The locks were compiled with the pip-compile commands of scripts/compile-dependency-locks.sh in the existing backend development image, without the script's image build. The release is 11 days old on this date and below the 30-day policy age: the project owner chose this version for the local evaluation, 2.4.3 (2026-10-06) is the newest release past the window, and no exception is recorded here because the ledger's reviewed_on date predates the release. Revisit before corporate admission. The PyPI vulnerabilities field and an OSV query on 2026-11-07 returned no advisory for 2.4.6. The hash-locked wheel installs and imports on the backend image; backend unit tests, ruff and strict mypy passed for the adapter. The local-egress gate reuses the admitted pinned nginx image, so no OCI coordinate changes.

2026-10-08: backend runtime dependencies for the dictionary workbook reader and the single-question Excel report (data-dictionary/PRDs/001-dictionary-management Decision 1, data-dictionary/PRDs/004-question-analysis Dependency impact): direct runtime pins openpyxl 3.1.5 (PyPI upload 2024-06-28, MIT; openpyxl-3.1.5-py2.py3-none-any.whl sha256 5282c12b107bffeef825f4617dc029afaf41d0ea60823bbb665ef3079dc79de2 and openpyxl-3.1.5.tar.gz sha256 cf0e3cf56142039133628b5acffe8ef0c12bc902d2aadd3e0fe5878dc08d1050) and defusedxml 0.7.1 (PyPI upload 2021-03-08, PSF-2.0; defusedxml-0.7.1-py2.py3-none-any.whl sha256 a352e7e428770286cc899e2542b6cdaedb2b4953ff269a210103ec58f6198a61 and defusedxml-0.7.1.tar.gz sha256 1bb3032db185915b62d7c6209c5a8792be6a32ab2fedacc84e01b52c51aa3e69; openpyxl parses workbook XML with it when it is installed) in app/backend/requirements.in; their locked transitive et-xmlfile 2.0.0 (PyPI upload 2024-10-25, MIT; et_xmlfile-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl sha256 7a91720bc756843502c3b7504c77b8fe44217c85c537d85037f0f536151b2caa and et_xmlfile-2.0.0.tar.gz sha256 dab3f4764309081ce75662649be815c4c9081e88f0837825f90fd28317d4da54). The three versions and digests are the source application's requirements.lock pins, so the byte-for-byte parity of the dictionary parser and the report holds. scripts/compile-dependency-locks.sh regenerated requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt and requirements-llm.txt in the backend development image on top of the OpenTelemetry, httpx and cryptography pins above; only these three packages and their PyPI digests are added, no other pin changes. OSV queries for PyPI openpyxl 3.1.5, defusedxml 0.7.1 and et-xmlfile 2.0.0 on 2026-10-08 returned no advisory. Compatibility: backend unit tests, ruff, black, isort and strict mypy (openpyxl has no inline types; mypy treats its modules as untyped like PyYAML) passed with the regenerated locks.

2026-10-08: security update of two locked transitive dependencies of the optional LLM set. urllib3 2.8.0 (PyPI 2026-09-15, MIT, upstream tag 2.8.0 at b1d30ab61fe0db8f11092805e8c5ac43e091064a) replaces 2.7.0 and langgraph-sdk 0.4.4 (PyPI 2026-08-27, MIT, upstream tag sdk==0.4.4 at d5f4b2aa960940effc8430165ab3604038e817af) replaces 0.4.3 in app/backend/requirements-llm.txt. urllib3 2.8.0 fixes CVE-2026-97687 (GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77, HIGH, CVSS 4.0 7.6: the TLS configuration of an HTTPS proxy is ignored or overridden by the target server's), CVE-2026-97689 (GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw, HIGH, CVSS 4.0 8.9: HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() buffer an unbounded chunk-size line in memory) and CVE-2026-97688 (GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g, MODERATE, CVSS 4.0 6.9: chunked Deflate streaming can loop forever); langgraph-sdk 0.4.4 fixes CVE-2026-104873 (GHSA-fvww-7h3r-vfhp, HIGH, CVSS 4.0 7.6: actions= on the resource-scoped custom auth decorators registers the handler for every action of the resource). Each is the first release without its advisories. requests 2.34.2 (urllib3<3,>=1.26) and langgraph 1.2.11 (langgraph-sdk<0.5.0,>=0.4.2) reach them only as locked transitive dependencies, so no parent pin, app/backend/requirements-llm.in entry or inventory coordinate changes, and langgraph-sdk stays undeclared as the governed LLM orchestration PRD requires. scripts/compile-dependency-locks.sh in a fresh project resolved both versions while requirements-llm.in named them for one run, then reproduced the same lock byte for byte from the unchanged requirements-llm.in; only the two pins and their PyPI digests change, requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt are byte-identical, and OSV reports no advisory on any package of the new lock. urllib3 2.8.0 is younger than 30 days and stays a security exception until 2026-10-15; langgraph-sdk 0.4.4 is older than 30 days. Release, advisory, lock update and generated-project checks: docs/evidence/2026-10-08-llm-lock-security-update.md in factory source.

2026-10-02: security update of the nginx base. nginx:1.31.6-alpine-slim@sha256:f761b94f2cb9e8e05e2943d5f773609596113ef69b54e2433a996d109a8f78b7 (nginx 1.31.6, Alpine 3.24.2 OCI index, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, published 2026-09-23) replaces nginx:alpine@sha256:4a73073bd557c65b759505da037898b61f1be6cbcc3c2c3aeac22d2a470c1752 in the frontend release image, the local Compose proxy and the image workflow. The previous base carried 18 HIGH findings in OpenSSL, libuuid, libexpat and pcre2; the slim variant ships neither libexpat nor libuuid. No published official nginx Alpine image carries pcre2 10.49-r0 (CVE-2026-103111, HIGH, Alpine package published 2026-10-01), so app/infra/locks/nginx-alpine-packages.lock pins it by exact version and SHA-256 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 and app/infra/Dockerfile.frontend.release installs it without consulting a repository. The generated frontend release image scans with 0 findings at every severity on both architectures. Evidence: docs/evidence/2026-10-02-nginx-pcre2-security-update.md in factory source.
